result.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
result.summary: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. We characterize search through evolutionary optimization and examine its reliability through continual PAC-learning. Under explicit assumptions, the analysis yields an expected generalization bound, a retention bound conditional on historical regression budgets, and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data. We examine how persistent harness revisions affect knowledge sharing and organizational workflows, with implications for scientific reliability, physical safety, and institutional accountability. Cases from prior work illustrate model--harness co-design, distributed execution, and plugin reuse. Reliable deployment requires continual validation as task distributions and evaluators change, with independent safeguards for learning, runtime privileges, and consequential actions. We provide a comprehensive 66-page discussion of related work, theory, algorithms, evaluation, applications, and the broader impact of Harness RSI, together with continuously updated code and supplementary materials, at https://github.com/zgcagi/Harness-RSI.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「harness 自我进化」形式化：模型权重固定，靠反馈驱动的修订持续更新 prompt、记忆、工作流与可执行组件，并给出进化搜索的期望泛化界、回归预算下的保留界与基于独立验证数据的准入规则，另附 66 页综述与开源材料。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「提案—验证—准入」流程与回归预算下的保留判据，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态或工作区更新何时被采纳、如何分配监督并避免信息坍缩；但论文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，联系属于概念层面的迁移猜想。
